_about: measured quantization degradation, per model. SOURCE, not derived: nothing
in this repo can compute it, because it takes running the same model at two
or more quants on the same benchmark at the same settings.
EMPTY ON PURPOSE. the sweeps that exist today cannot fill it: quantbench has
1269 scored trials across 15 configs, but only two models were run at more
than one quant and in both cases one arm has n<=2. a curve fitted to that
would be noise wearing a decimal point. the schema is here so a real sweep
drops in without touching the viewer.
a point is [bits per weight, retention], where retention is the score at
that quant over the score at the highest-precision arm of the SAME sweep --
same model, same benchmark, same samplers, same thinking level. anything
else is comparing two different measurements and calling the difference
quantization.
what a usable entry looks like:
"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731": {
"metric": "aider polyglot pass rate",
"trials": 580,
"ref": {"source": "unsloth", "url": "https://...", "captured": "2026-08-17"}
scripts/build-viewer validates these on the way through: bits per weight
ascending, retention in (0, 1], and at least two points. where a model has
no entry the page falls back to the median of the entries that do exist, and
to build-tables' fitted curve when there are fewer than MIN_CURVES of them.
the page says which of the three it used, every time.

ref.note: ten rungs of mean kl divergence against bf16, published as a chart on unsloth's docs site rather than on the hf card, which is why fetch-quant-sweeps cannot reach it and this entry is hand-written. the same table publishes top-1 agreement: 77.325% at UD-IQ1_S rising to 94.122% at Q8_0, with UD-IQ4_XS 89.554 and UD-Q4_K_XL 92.255. all ten sizes match the bytes fetch-gguf-sizes measured, so the ladder is of exactly these files
